title: Experiential Onboarding and Role Certification Playbook
author: Marin Alvarez
body:
Summary

This playbook defines an experiential onboarding program that pairs structured milestones (30/60/90) with a formal role certification assessment at week 12 (or on completion of the role-specific curriculum). The program combines hiring-to-handoff procedures, manager and buddy responsibilities, performance calibration, and templates for feedback cycles.

Scope
- New full-time hires and internal role transfers where the role has a documented certification path.
- Applies to engineering, product, and support functions; adapted variants for sales and GTM teams available as appendices.

Principles
- Active learning: 60% hands-on, 40% observation/reading in the first 90 days.
- Clear success criteria: defined, measurable rubrics per competency.
- Manager accountability: timely feedback and decisions at 30/60/90.
- Fast failure-safe: early signals trigger role adjustments or additional support, not surprises.

Program flow (high level)
1. Offer accepted -> Preboarding (days -14 to 0): account access, equipment shipment, first-day agenda. Owner: People Ops; SLA: 72 hours to provision core accounts.
2. Day 0-14: Immersion sprint (product, codebase, architecture primers, stakeholder 1:1s). Owner: Hiring manager + buddy.
3. Day 15-60: Experiential assignments (low-risk tickets, paired work, shadowing). Weekly 1:1 + weekly peer sync.
4. Day 61-90+: Certification sprint (capstone assignment, cross-team demo, 360 feedback). Final outcome: Certified / Conditional / Not-Yet-Certified. Decision owner: Manager + People Ops.

30/60/90 checkpoints and deliverables
- 30-day: Basic competency checklist (access, environment, first PR merged, two stakeholder 1:1s). Decision: On-track/Needs Support.
- 60-day: Intermediate competency (ownership of a small feature or deliverable, documented runbook). Decision: On-track / Extra Coaching Required.
- 90-day: Certification decision. Evidence: capstone deliverable, 360 feedback, manager rubric. Decision options: Certified, Conditional (30-day remediation), Not-Yet-Certified -> escalate to People Ops and manager for next steps.

Certification rubric (example for software engineer)
- Technical correctness (scale 1-5): code quality, tests, infra hygiene.
- Ownership & delivery (1-5): scope understanding, estimates, drive.
- Collaboration & communication (1-5): cross-team interactions, async clarity.
- Product judgement (1-5): prioritization, impact orientation.
Pass threshold: aggregate >= 14/20 and no category below 3.

Week-by-week sample schedule (first 12 weeks)
| Week | Focus | Owner | Key deliverable |
|------|-------|-------|-----------------|
| -2 to 0 | Preboarding | People Ops | Hardware + access checklist completed |
| 0 | Orientation | People Ops/Manager | Team kickoff + account access confirmed |
| 1-2 | Codebase primer | Buddy/Manager | First PR merged + doc update |
| 3-6 | Paired work | Manager/Buddy | Small feature shipped + metrics baseline |
| 7-10 | Independent delivery | Manager | Ownership of a live change + monitoring |
| 11-12 | Capstone & demo | Manager + Cross-team | Final demo + 360 feedback collected |

Manager responsibilities (checklist)
- Pre-hire: provide role profile, 30/60/90 success criteria, and onboarding tasks to People Ops.
- Day 0: 1:1 within first 48 hours and schedule weekly 1:1s.
- Provide timely feedback: use the shared rubric and submit 30/60 notes to People Ops.
- Run the certification decision meeting at week 12 with People Ops and at least two cross-functional reviewers.

Buddy responsibilities
- Shadow on day 0, pair on first PR, be available for 2 office-hours weekly in first 60 days, maintain a public checklist for the new hire.

Feedback cadence and templates
- Weekly quick pulse (asynchronous): 5-minute update in the team channel using the prompt: "This week I shipped X; blocked on Y; ask: Z".
- 30/60 reflective self-assessment: short form (3 bullets per competency).
- 360 collection: manager requests feedback from at least 3 peers (one cross-team) via standard form.

Sample manager email (30-day check-in)
Subject: 30-day check-in: [New Hire Name]
Body:
Hi [Name],

Congrats on completing your first 30 days. Please find a quick agenda for our check-in:
1) Wins and blockers
2) Review 30-day checklist
3) Plan for next 30 days

Please bring your short self-assessment.

Best,
[Manager]

Decisioning and escalation process
- If the hire is "Not-Yet-Certified": the manager and People Ops create a 30-day remediation plan that includes measurable checkpoints and weekly 1:1s.
- If after remediation the outcome is still Not-Yet-Certified, People Ops convenes a review panel (manager, People Ops, cross-functional lead) to determine employment outcome and transition support.

Operational metrics (tracked in People Ops dashboard)
- Time to first PR merged (target <= 14 days)
- Fraction of hires certified at 12 weeks (target >= 85%)
- Manager completion rate of 30/60/90 notes (target >= 95%)
- New hire NPS at week 6 and week 12 (target >= 8/10)

Tooling and artifacts
- Onboarding checklist (Confluence template link): /confluence/templates/onboarding-checklist
- Certification rubric (spreadsheet): internal drive link (people-ops/onboarding/rubrics)
- 360 feedback form: /forms/people-ops/role-cert-360

Appendices
A. Role-specific certification examples (ENG/Product/CS)
B. Short remediation template (objectives, success metrics, owner, weekly checkpoints)
C. Customizations for returnships and short-term contractors (timeline adjustments and benefit differences)

Related policies and references
- Hiring & offer approval policy: /confluence/people-ops/offer-approval-policy
- Performance improvement policy: /confluence/people-ops/performance-and-pip-guidance

Owners and maintenance
- Playbook owner: People Ops - Onboarding Programs (Marin Alvarez).
- Review cadence: Annual review in Q4 or when company headcount policy changes.

Contact
